statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-116321 (PostgreSQL unterminated name value discloses server memory) is fixed upstream in PostgreSQL 18.7 for major version 18. The PostgreSQL security page, https://www.postgresql.org/support/security/CVE-2026-116321/, lists 18.7 as the fixed release for 18, the 18.7 release notes, https://www.postgresql.org/docs/release/18.7/, list this CVE, and the CVE record, https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-116321, lists 18 as affected before 18.7. The fix on the REL_18_STABLE branch is commit https://github.com/postgres/postgres/commit/b3ef92518c57d8db63ac18b4adcf585da90e0673, which carries the trailer "Security: CVE-2026-116321", is contained in the REL_18_7 tag and not in REL_18_6, and changes array_set_element() in src/backend/utils/adt/arrayfuncs.c so that element assignment can no longer set the final, terminating byte of a "name" value and rejects an invalidly encoded result. Alpine's postgresql18 18.7-r0 on the 3.23-stable branch upgrades to the upstream 18.7 release and lists CVE-2026-116321 under 18.7-r0 in its secfixes: https://github.com/alpinelinux/aports/blob/59a1f1d230675807d5a95a0c1e57ba5d640ba039/main/postgresql18/APKBUILD. None of the Alpine patches applied in that APKBUILD change the files the fix touches. The DHI postgresql18 18.7-r0 packages for Alpine 3.23 are built from that APKBUILD and the upstream PostgreSQL 18.7 source tarball. The DHI Alpine 3.23 package repository (main and security, x86_64 and aarch64) publishes packages built from source postgresql18 at 18.1-r0, 18.2-r0, 18.3-r0, 18.4-r0, 18.6-r0 and 18.7-r0. The vulnerable code is in the postgres server binary, usr/libexec/postgresql18/postgres, in the postgresql18 package. In the 18.7-r0 build the postgres server binary reports PostgreSQL 18.7 on both x86_64 and aarch64, and in each earlier build (18.1-r0, 18.2-r0, 18.3-r0, 18.4-r0 and 18.6-r0) it reports that older 18.x release on both architectures. The earlier builds are upstream releases before 18.7, so they are affected; 18.7-r0 and later carry the fix.

PostgreSQL fixed CVE-2026-116321, improper null termination in array element assignment of name values, which discloses server memory, in 17.12 (https://www.postgresql.org/support/security/CVE-2026-116321/, https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-116321, https://www.postgresql.org/docs/release/17.12/). Earlier 17 releases are affected. The server binary in this owner's 17.12-0 build and in its rebuild of Debian's 17.12-0+deb13u1 reports PostgreSQL 17.12 on amd64 and arm64, so both carry the fix. The 17.11-1 build and the current rebuild of Debian's 17.11-0+deb13u1 report PostgreSQL 17.11, and the earlier rebuilds of Debian's 17.10-0+deb13u1 and 17.11-0+deb13u1, no longer in the repository, package PostgreSQL 17.10 and 17.11. All of these are affected and sort below 17.12-0.
